question.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-4{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution $$ {X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}=\frac{6}{s}-\frac{2}{s-4},\,{X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}=\frac{3}{s}+\frac{1}{s-4}. $$ Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
$x(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,\,+\,\,$ {{field-2}} $\,\,{e}^{4t}$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to ${X}_{1}(s)$ and ${X}_{2}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{1}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{6}{s}-\frac{2}{s-4}\} \\  & =6{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}-2{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =6\cdot 1-2{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =6-2{e}^{4t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}\{{X}_{2}(s)\} \\  & ={L}^{-1}\{\frac{3}{s}+\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =3{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s}\}+{L}^{-1}\{\frac{1}{s-4}\} \\  & =3\cdot 1+{e}^{4\cdot t} \\  & =3+{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6-2{e}^{4t} \\ 3+{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}
$$
